nutritional_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Pair starchy carbohydrates with 10–15g of viscous soluble fiber (chia seeds, oats, psyllium, or whole lentils) and replace refined sweets with whole fruits to buffer postprandial glucose absorption.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_early: Post-meal lethargy, reactive hypoglycemia (energy crashes 2 hours after eating), and frequent carbohydrate cravings.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Exhaustion of pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion, progressive fasting hyperglycemia, and microvascular injury (diabetic retinopathy and nephropathy).

nutritional_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Limit added salt and processed snacks to keep sodium below 2,000 mg/day; boost potassium-dense foods (spinach, bottle gourd, lentils, coconut water) to exceed 3,500 mg/day.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_early: Subtle fluid retention, transient blood pressure elevations, and increased arterial wall tension.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Progressive arterial wall remodeling and stiffening, left ventricular concentric hypertrophy, and substantially elevated risk of hemorrhagic stroke.

nutritional_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Moderate cooking fats (ghee, butter, palm oil) to <10% of total calories; substitute with cold-pressed monounsaturated fats (mustard oil, olive oil, sesame oil, nuts).
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_early: Downregulation of hepatic LDL receptors, leading to higher circulating concentrations of ApoB atherogenic particles.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Subendothelial cholesterol deposition, formation of fibrous atheromatous plaques in coronary and carotid arteries, and heightened myocardial infarction risk.

nutritional_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Increase intake of unpolished grains (millets, brown rice), leafy greens, and whole legumes to reach your daily target (≥28g females, ≥38g males).
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_early: Sluggish gastrointestinal transit, reduced short-chain fatty acid (butyrate) synthesis, and blunted postprandial satiety.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Degradation of the protective gut mucosal layer, subclinical endotoxemia (leaky gut), systemic low-grade inflammation, and increased colorectal disease risk.

nutritional_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Ensure 20–30g of high-biological-value protein per main meal (paneer, tofu, dal with rice, eggs, fish, or sprouted moong) to maintain at least 0.8–1.0 g/kg body weight.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_early: Delayed muscle recovery after exertion, mild afternoon fatigue, and gradual decline in basal metabolic calorie burn.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Accelerated skeletal muscle wasting (sarcopenia), physical frailty, reduced functional mobility, and decreased whole-body glucose disposal capacity.

nutritional_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Consume calcium-rich foods (curd, ragi, sesame seeds, fortified milk) and magnesium sources (almonds, pumpkin seeds, green leafy vegetables) daily.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_early: Occasional muscle cramps, neuromuscular irritability, and compensatory bone remodeling to sustain serum calcium levels.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Progressive loss of skeletal bone mineral density (osteopenia transitioning to osteoporosis), increased fracture susceptibility, and vascular wall calcification.

nutritional_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Combine iron-rich plant foods (spinach, lentils, dates) with natural ascorbic acid (fresh lemon juice, amla) to boost non-heme iron absorption threefold.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_early: Mild exertional shortness of breath, diminished exercise endurance, and cognitive brain fog.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Microcytic hypochromic anemia, chronic tissue hypoxia, impaired cardiac output, and compromised immune cell surveillance.

nutritional_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Add half a fresh lemon over cooked curries, enjoy citrus fruits, or consume raw amla/guava daily to meet the 75–100 mg/day antioxidant threshold.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_early: Suboptimal collagen synthesis, reduced microvascular capillary resilience, and delayed minor wound healing.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Heightened oxidative modification of circulating LDL particles, accelerating endothelial dysfunction and vascular plaque initiation.

nutritional_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Keep alcohol consumption within safe limits (≤1 standard drink/day for women, ≤2 for men) with at least 3–4 consecutive alcohol-free days weekly.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_early: Transient elevation of hepatic triglycerides, suppression of nocturnal REM sleep, and temporary morning blood pressure surges.
nutritional_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Progressive hepatic steatosis (metabolic liver disease), persistent sympathetic tone elevation, and cardiometabolic dyslipidemia.

weight_related_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Align daily calorie intake within ±150 kcal of your Mifflin-St Jeor TDEE; for gradual fat loss, introduce a structured 300–400 kcal deficit via mindful portion control.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_early: Positive caloric storage expanding subcutaneous adipose reserves, mild abdominal bloating, and increased insulin secretion.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Ectopic visceral lipid accumulation directly surrounding the liver, heart, and pancreas, driving Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD).

weight_related_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Adopt a consistent calorie-controlled whole-food diet combined with daily brisk walking to gradually bring BMI toward the 18.5–24.9 kg/m² healthy range.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_early: Increased mechanical load on knee and hip joints, mild exertional dyspnea, and subclinical elevation of systemic inflammatory markers (hs-CRP).
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Chronic systemic adipokine toxicity (elevated TNF-α, IL-6), accelerated joint cartilage degradation (osteoarthritis), and marked peripheral insulin receptor downregulation.

weight_related_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Incorporate progressive resistance training (bodyweight squats, resistance bands, or light weights) 2–3 times weekly alongside adequate protein intake (1.0–1.2 g/kg).
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_early: Normal or high scale weight masking a loss of functional muscle mass, accompanied by early fatigue during daily chores.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Severe metabolic decline where lower muscle mass burns fewer resting calories, locking the body into rapid fat regain and frailty.

weight_related_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Stand or walk for 2–3 minutes every 45–60 minutes of sitting; consider a height-adjustable standing desk or walking meetings.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_early: Suppression of muscle lipoprotein lipase (LPL) activity, leading to slower post-meal lipid and glucose clearance from circulation.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Lower-extremity venous stasis, skeletal muscle insulin resistance, and significantly elevated all-cause cardiovascular mortality.

weight_related_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Accumulate at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise (brisk walking at 5 km/h) or 75 minutes of vigorous exercise weekly to meet the 600 MET-min guideline.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_early: Gradual decrease in maximal oxygen uptake (VO2 max) and diminished cardiac stroke volume efficiency.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Loss of skeletal muscle mitochondrial density, blunted non-insulin-mediated GLUT4 glucose uptake, and arterial stiffening.

weight_related_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Integrate purposeful active travel—such as taking the stairs, parking further away, or walking for short neighborhood errands (aim for 20–30 min/day).
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_early: Low non-exercise activity thermogenesis (NEAT), reducing total daily baseline calorie burn.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Decreased peripheral circulation, reduced lymphatic drainage, and heightened vulnerability to weight creep over time.

weight_related_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Maintain a regular sleep schedule aiming for 7.0–8.5 hours nightly; avoid screen exposure and heavy meals within 2 hours of bedtime.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_early: Acute hormonal disruption: elevated morning cortisol, increased hunger hormone ghrelin (+28%), and suppressed satiety hormone leptin (-18%).
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Chronic circadian insulin resistance, habitual evening hyperphagia (cravings for hyper-palatable foods), and blunted metabolic flexibility.

weight_related_risk_stratification.mitigation_action: Optimize sleep hygiene (cool, dark room; minimize alcohol before sleep); if snoring or waking gasping occurs, seek clinical evaluation for obstructive sleep apnea.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_early: Frequent nocturnal micro-arousals triggering nighttime sympathetic nervous system surges and unrefreshing sleep.
weight_related_risk_stratification.progression_advanced: Sustained nocturnal hypoxemia, loss of physiological blood pressure dipping at night, morning hypertension, and long-term cardiac strain.
